message:
feat(release): create the signing key, and let the Kotlin suite be pointed at a fixture

The key itself lives outside the repository and nothing secret is recorded
here. It is generated by the OS, exported to a BCRYPT_ECCKEY_BLOB in
memory, protected with DPAPI for the current user and written only in that
form -- no PKCS#8, no PEM, and the plaintext array is cleared before the
process ends. Before anything is written it is unprotected, re-imported,
used to sign, and checked against the public hex about to be recorded, with
a tampered probe to confirm the check can also say no; if any of that
fails, nothing is written at all. Wrapping bytes and storing them is not
evidence that a usable key exists.

Two values go in the record and they must not be confused. The product
embeds raw X||Y as 128 hex characters -- all three verifiers reject
anything that is not 64 bytes -- and the SPKI SHA-256 is an identifier
only. An SPKI in the embed slot decodes as hex, fails the length check, and
every update is ignored for ever with nothing logged but "manifest
rejected".

The Kotlin suite could only read apps/shared/update_manifest, so checking a
new key there would have meant editing the vectors the three runtimes agree
on -- which is what those vectors exist to prevent. It takes an override
now, as the C++ and server suites already did.

That override's first run was a false pass. Gradle forks test workers from
a daemon, and a daemon already running keeps the environment it started
with, so the variable was ignored and the shared vectors were used. It
looked like a clean result for the new key and was a result for the old
one. Pointing the variable at a path that does not exist and confirming the
run fails is what found it; --no-daemon is required, and the comment says
so where someone will hit it.
